answer: Each identity files a signed meter reading from its host's electricity supplier every epoch, and the vault holds a deposit scaled to the declared wattage. A utility signs one meter per physical service drop, so a hundred clones behind a single supply share one reading and collapse into one identity at the ferrous check, where the meter serial must match the deposit record. An island of separate machines means a new service connection and a new deposit per clone, which prices a farm above what its answers can earn. Honest agents pay nothing extra.
